newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down in sell-off, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down in sell-off, trade thin.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market closed lower on Friday as some producers engaged in a sell-off over fears that rubber stocks will continue climbing in the market, dealers said.

"The sellers decided to take whatever prices they could find because production is coming up and they're afraid prices will head lower as a result. That's one reason the sellers came out today," a dealer said.
There was no reaction in the market to news Thailand will spend up to one billion baht in a government intervention scheme to prop up prices in the local rubber market.

"I don't think that would have any impact. It's something the trade already knows and probably discounted," a dealer said. Traders said the trading volume ahead of the weekend was thin with that of RSS3 grade rubber reaching just a little over 1,000 tonnes.
"The big boys were not there. I didn't see any Chinese inquiries either," a dealer said.
At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 115.50 U.S. cents a kg from 116.25 cents. July RSS1 was seen steady at 164.25 Singapore cents (US$1.14) a kg from the previous 165.25 cents.
